title.title: Zilber–Pink for abelian varieties and curves in $\mathcal{A}_2$
title.subtitle: Claim: unlikely intersections are finite, for subvarieties of abelian varieties and curves in $\mathcal{A}_2$

beats.text: A subvariety should meet special subvarieties in too-small codimension only finitely often
The curve case in $\mathcal{A}_2$ comes in three components, one paper each
Over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ only, and nothing is effective

achievement.label: Zilber–Pink conjecture (Zilber 2002, Pink 2005)
achievement.context: Before: curves in abelian varieties (Habegger–Pila 2016); $\mathcal{A}_2$ curves under boundary hypotheses
achievement.note: Over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, not $\mathbb{C}$; the abelian theorem is non-effective

plain: Shapes should cross special sub-shapes in surprising ways only finitely often; this proves it in two settings

steps: Suppose infinitely many unlikely points spread everywhere
Sort them into height levels and rescale each level
Their limit needs a direction that tangent positivity forbids
